p01.text: Mijn leven was altijd heel eenvoudig. Eten, slapen en af en toe iets van de tafel duwen, gewoon om te zien of de zwaartekracht nog werkt. Tot die ene regenachtige avond. Er tikte iets tegen het raam. Een uil, groot als een kussen, met een brief in zijn snavel.
p01.narration: My life was always very simple. Eat, sleep, and now and then push something off the table, just to check that gravity still works. Until that one rainy evening. Something tapped on the window. An owl, as big as a cushion, with a letter in its beak.

shots.prompt: Characters in this shot: Marcel (the grey British Shorthair cat with orange eyes, wearing tiny round wire-rimmed glasses). A cosy living room in the evening. Marcel sits on a wooden dining table and pushes a glass towards the edge with one paw, looking completely innocent. Warm lamplight.

Characters in this shot: Marcel (the grey British Shorthair cat with orange eyes, wearing tiny round wire-rimmed glasses); Professor Otto (a large, wise old eagle-owl with fluffy ear tufts and amber eyes). Night, rain streaming down a living-room window. Marcel sits on the windowsill and stares in surprise at the glass: outside on the wet ledge, Professor Otto holds a sealed cream-coloured envelope in his beak. Cold blue moonlight outside, warm lamplight inside.

p02.text: Hij liet de brief vallen, precies in de kattenbak. Natuurlijk. Ik viste hem eruit en las de gouden letters: Geachte heer Marcel, u bent uitverkoren voor de Whiskerwood Academie voor Magische Katten. Reclame, dacht ik. Maar toen vlogen er tien brieven door het kattenluik, daarna vijftig, en binnen een minuut lag de hele keuken vol.
p02.narration: He dropped the letter right into the litter box. Of course. I fished it out and read the golden words: Dear Mister Marcel, you have been chosen for the Whiskerwood Academy for Magical Cats. Junk mail, I thought. But then ten letters flew in through the cat flap, then fifty, and within a minute the whole kitchen was full.

shots.prompt: Characters in this shot: Marcel (the grey British Shorthair cat with orange eyes, wearing tiny round wire-rimmed glasses). A sealed cream-coloured envelope tumbles down and lands right in a cat litter box on a tiled floor. Marcel sits next to it, looking deeply offended. Soft night light.

Characters in this shot: Marcel (the grey British Shorthair cat with orange eyes, wearing tiny round wire-rimmed glasses). A kitchen at night: dozens of cream-coloured envelopes fly in through the cat flap in the back door and swirl through the air, piling up on the floor and counters. Marcel stands in the middle of the storm of letters, holding one opened letter, eyes wide. No writing on the envelopes.

p03.text: Toen ik opkeek, zat de uil op de keukentafel, alsof hij er altijd al had gezeten. Professor Otto, stelde hij zich voor, directeur van Whiskerwood. Je bent geen gewone kat, zei hij, je bent een tovenaar die het nog niet weet. Om drie uur 's nachts, wanneer alle katten ter wereld plots beginnen te rennen, gaat het kattenluik open naar een andere wereld. Ik keek naar de klok. Twee uur negenenvijftig.
p03.narration: When I looked up, the owl was sitting on the kitchen table, as if he had always been there. Professor Otto, he introduced himself, headmaster of Whiskerwood. You are no ordinary cat, he said, you are a wizard who doesn't know it yet. At three in the morning, when every cat in the world suddenly starts running, the cat flap opens into another world. I looked at the clock. Two fifty-nine.

shots.prompt: Characters in this shot: Professor Otto (a large, wise old eagle-owl with fluffy ear tufts and amber eyes); Marcel (the grey British Shorthair cat with orange eyes, wearing tiny round wire-rimmed glasses). A dark kitchen lit by a single lamp, envelopes scattered everywhere. Professor Otto perches on the kitchen table among the letters, looking solemnly at Marcel, who sits opposite him, eyes wide behind his tiny glasses.

Characters in this shot: Marcel (the grey British Shorthair cat with orange eyes, wearing tiny round wire-rimmed glasses). A round kitchen clock on a dark wall shows one minute to three. Below it, Marcel sits on the floor in moonlight, looking up at the clock, the cat flap in the back door beside him.

p04.text: Om exact drie uur begon het kattenluik te gloeien. Ik rende, zoals elke kat om die tijd rent, en dook erdoor. Ik viel door een tunnel van sterren, draaide drie keer om mijn as en landde op mijn pootjes. Natuurlijk. Ik stond in een zaal zo groot als tien huizen, met honderden kaarsen die gewoon in de lucht zweefden.
p04.narration: At exactly three o'clock, the cat flap began to glow. I ran, the way every cat runs at that hour, and dived through it. I fell through a tunnel of stars, spun around three times, and landed on my feet. Of course. I was standing in a hall as big as ten houses, with hundreds of candles simply floating in the air.

shots.prompt: Characters in this shot: Marcel (the grey British Shorthair cat with orange eyes, wearing tiny round wire-rimmed glasses). A dark kitchen at night: Marcel dives head first through the cat flap in the back door, which glows with bright golden light; sparkles burst around him, motion blur.

Characters in this shot: Marcel (the grey British Shorthair cat with orange eyes, wearing tiny round wire-rimmed glasses). Marcel tumbles out of a swirl of stars and golden light and lands on the stone floor of a huge castle hall with long wooden tables and hundreds of real candles floating in the air. Wonder, warm candlelight.

p05.text: Naast me landden nog twee nieuwe leerlingen. Hazel, een egeltje met een stapel boeken die groter was dan zijzelf, die me meteen vertelde dat ze alle boeken van de school al gelezen had. En Bruno, een bassetpup met oren tot op de grond, die alleen wilde weten of er hier ook ontbijt was. Ik wist meteen: dit worden mijn vrienden. Of mijn fans.
p05.narration: Next to me, two more new students landed. Hazel, a hedgehog with a pile of books bigger than herself, who immediately told me she had already read every book in the school. And Bruno, a basset puppy with ears down to the floor, who only wanted to know if there was breakfast here. I knew right away: these would be my friends. Or my fans.

shots.prompt: Characters in this shot: Marcel (the grey British Shorthair cat with orange eyes, wearing tiny round wire-rimmed glasses); Hazel (a small hedgehog who always carries a tiny stack of old books); Bruno (a clumsy, cheerful basset hound puppy with very long ears). In the candlelit hall, Hazel and Bruno tumble onto the stone floor next to Marcel in a little cloud of golden sparkles; Hazel clutches her tiny stack of books, Bruno sniffs the air hungrily.

Characters in this shot: Marcel (the grey British Shorthair cat with orange eyes, wearing tiny round wire-rimmed glasses); Hazel (a small hedgehog who always carries a tiny stack of old books); Bruno (a clumsy, cheerful basset hound puppy with very long ears). The three of them side by side, seen from behind, looking up at the enormous hall full of floating candles.

p06.text: Midden in de zaal lag een oude, versleten hoed op een kruk. Professor Otto zette hem op mijn kop, en de hoed begon te praten, met een stem als een krakende kast. Hmm, zei hij. Veel moed, nog meer honger, en een verrassend talent om overal te slapen. Huis Dutje, riep hij. De hele zaal applaudisseerde, behalve Huis Dutje zelf, want die lagen allemaal te slapen.
p06.narration: In the middle of the hall, an old, worn hat lay on a stool. Professor Otto placed it on my head, and the hat began to talk, in a voice like a creaking cupboard. Hmm, it said. Plenty of courage, even more hunger, and a surprising talent for sleeping anywhere. House Nap, it shouted. The whole hall applauded, except House Nap itself, because they were all fast asleep.

shots.prompt: Characters in this shot: Professor Otto (a large, wise old eagle-owl with fluffy ear tufts and amber eyes); Marcel (the grey British Shorthair cat with orange eyes, wearing tiny round wire-rimmed glasses); the Hat (an old, patched, pointed wizard hat with a crease that looks like a mouth). In the centre of the candlelit hall, Professor Otto lowers the Hat onto Marcel's head with his talons; the Hat is far too big and slides down over one eye, its crease bent like a speaking mouth. Animal students watch from the long tables.
A long table at the side of the hall where a row of different animal students, cats, a badger and a sheep, sleep with their heads on the table, while the animals at the other tables cheer.

p07.text: Huis Dutje woont in de kelder, in één reusachtige mand waar iedereen twintig uur per dag slaapt. Ik voelde me meteen thuis. In mijn eerste les liet ik een sok zweven, wat volgens mij een record was. Hazel vond het matig. Zij had intussen in een stoffig boek ontdekt dat er in het kasteel iets verborgen lag: de Steen der Brokjes, die ervoor zorgt dat je etensbak nooit, maar dan ook nooit meer leeg raakt.
p07.narration: House Nap lives in the cellar, in one gigantic basket where everyone sleeps twenty hours a day. I felt at home straight away. In my first lesson I made a sock float, which I believe was a record. Hazel was not impressed. She had discovered in a dusty book that something was hidden in the castle: the Kibble Stone, which makes sure your food bowl never, ever runs empty again.

shots.prompt: Characters in this shot: Marcel (the grey British Shorthair cat with orange eyes, wearing tiny round wire-rimmed glasses); Bruno (a clumsy, cheerful basset hound puppy with very long ears). A vaulted castle cellar filled by one gigantic woven basket with soft blankets, where many cats and small animals sleep in a cosy heap. Marcel is curled up blissfully in the middle, Bruno snoring beside him. Warm candlelight.

Characters in this shot: Marcel (the grey British Shorthair cat with orange eyes, wearing tiny round wire-rimmed glasses); Hazel (a small hedgehog who always carries a tiny stack of old books). An old classroom with wooden desks: Marcel, one paw raised, makes a single striped sock float in the air, glowing faintly, looking extremely proud. Beside him Hazel, unimpressed, points at an old book showing a drawing of a small glowing red stone shaped like a piece of cat kibble. No readable writing.

p08.text: Op zaterdag speelden we Vliegvangen, op bezems, hoog boven het grasveld. Ik had nog nooit op een bezem gezeten, en dat was te zien. Toen zoemde de Gouden Vlieg langs mijn neus, het snelste beestje van de wereld. Maar ik heb jaren ervaring met vliegen. Ik ving hem in drie seconden, met mijn mond, en het hele stadion ontplofte. Alleen ik zag het: hoog op de noordtoren zat een zwarte vogel, die alles bekeek.
p08.narration: On Saturday we played Flycatch, on broomsticks, high above the lawn. I had never sat on a broomstick before, and it showed. Then the Golden Fly buzzed past my nose, the fastest creature in the world. But I have years of experience with flies. I caught it in three seconds, with my mouth, and the whole stadium exploded. Only I saw it: high on the north tower sat a black bird, watching everything.

shots.prompt: Characters in this shot: Marcel (the grey British Shorthair cat with orange eyes, wearing tiny round wire-rimmed glasses). A green castle lawn on a bright day, surrounded by tall wooden stands full of cheering animals. Marcel clings upside down underneath a wobbling broomstick high in the air, glasses askew, panicking; other cats on broomsticks fly around him.

Characters in this shot: Marcel (the grey British Shorthair cat with orange eyes, wearing tiny round wire-rimmed glasses); Corvus (a large, glossy black raven with piercing eyes). Marcel back on top of his broomstick, triumphant, a tiny glittering golden fly between his teeth, the stands behind him erupting in cheers. Far in the background, on top of a dark stone tower, the small silhouette of Corvus watches.

p09.text: Die nacht kon ik niet slapen, wat voor een kat echt uitzonderlijk is. In een vergeten lokaal vond ik een oude spiegel. Ik zag er niet mezelf in, maar wat ik het allerliefste wilde: een etensbak die nooit leeg raakt, een eeuwige zonnestraal, en Hazel en Bruno naast me. Professor Otto landde naast me en zei zacht dat een volle buik nog geen gelukkig hart is. Ik begreep er niets van. Toen nog niet.
p09.narration: That night I couldn't sleep, which for a cat is truly exceptional. In a forgotten classroom, I found an old mirror. I didn't see myself in it, but what I wanted most of all: a food bowl that never runs empty, an eternal sunbeam, and Hazel and Bruno beside me. Professor Otto landed next to me and said softly that a full belly is not the same as a happy heart. I didn't understand a word of it. Not yet.

A dusty forgotten classroom at night, silver moonlight through a tall window. A tall ornate mirror with a carved golden frame stands with a white sheet half pulled off it. Marcel sits in front of it, looking up, curious.

Characters in this shot: Marcel (the grey British Shorthair cat with orange eyes, wearing tiny round wire-rimmed glasses); Hazel (a small hedgehog who always carries a tiny stack of old books); Bruno (a clumsy, cheerful basset hound puppy with very long ears); Professor Otto (a large, wise old eagle-owl with fluffy ear tufts and amber eyes). The mirror's reflection shows a sunny dream instead of the dark room: a golden bowl overflowing with kibble, and Marcel curled up in a warm sunbeam with Hazel and Bruno beside him. The real Marcel sits in front of the mirror in the moonlit dark, and Professor Otto perches on a dusty desk beside him with a gentle, wise look.

p10.text: De nacht daarna sleepte Hazel ons mee naar de verboden gang op de derde verdieping. Achter een zware deur lag een luik in de vloer. En op dat luik zat een hamster. Een gigantische hamster, zo groot als een zetel, met wangen vol geheimen. Bruno rolde zich meteen op zijn rug, en de hamster, totaal ontwapend, begon zijn buik te kriebelen.
p10.narration: The next night, Hazel dragged us to the forbidden corridor on the third floor. Behind a heavy door was a trapdoor in the floor. And on that trapdoor sat a hamster. A gigantic hamster, as big as a sofa, with cheeks full of secrets. Bruno immediately rolled onto his back, and the hamster, completely disarmed, started tickling his belly.

shots.prompt: Characters in this shot: Marcel (the grey British Shorthair cat with orange eyes, wearing tiny round wire-rimmed glasses); Hazel (a small hedgehog who always carries a tiny stack of old books); Bruno (a clumsy, cheerful basset hound puppy with very long ears); the giant hamster (a gigantic fluffy golden hamster, as big as a sofa). A heavy old wooden door creaks open. Marcel, Hazel holding a tiny candle, and Bruno peek into a dark stone room where the giant hamster sits on a wooden trapdoor in the floor, cheeks bulging, staring at them. The giant hamster is truly as big as a sofa.

Characters in this shot: Bruno (a clumsy, cheerful basset hound puppy with very long ears); the giant hamster (a gigantic fluffy golden hamster, as big as a sofa); Marcel (the grey British Shorthair cat with orange eyes, wearing tiny round wire-rimmed glasses); Hazel (a small hedgehog who always carries a tiny stack of old books). Bruno lies on his back while the giant hamster happily tickles his belly with one paw; Marcel and Hazel watch from the doorway in disbelief. Moody torchlight, comedic.

p11.text: Toen hoorde ik vleugels boven ons. Corvus, de raaf, ooit de beste leerling van Whiskerwood en nu de meest gevreesde. Ik wil de Steen der Brokjes, fluisterde hij, niet om zelf op te eten, maar om alle etensbakken ter wereld voor altijd leeg te maken, behalve de mijne. Voor zonsopgang kom ik hem halen. En weg was hij, met achterlating van één zwarte veer.
p11.narration: Then I heard wings above us. Corvus, the raven, once the best student at Whiskerwood and now the most feared. I want the Kibble Stone, he whispered, not to eat it myself, but to make every food bowl in the world empty forever, except mine. Before sunrise, I will come for it. And he was gone, leaving behind a single black feather.

shots.prompt: Characters in this shot: Corvus (a large, glossy black raven with piercing eyes); Marcel (the grey British Shorthair cat with orange eyes, wearing tiny round wire-rimmed glasses); Hazel (a small hedgehog who always carries a tiny stack of old books); Bruno (a clumsy, cheerful basset hound puppy with very long ears). The dark stone room. Corvus perches on a high stone arch above Marcel, Hazel and Bruno, wings half spread, eyes glinting in the torchlight; the three look up in fear. Cold blue shadows, ominous.

Characters in this shot: Corvus (a large, glossy black raven with piercing eyes). Close-up of Corvus's sharp beak and piercing eye in the dark, as if whispering a terrible secret, a single black feather drifting down past him. Cold blue light.

p12.text: We renden naar Professor Otto, helemaal boven in de toren. Hij sliep. Ik riep, Hazel klopte, en Bruno blafte zo hard dat het stof van het plafond viel. Professor Otto opende één oog, mompelde dat uilen 's nachts werken, maar niet op dinsdag, en sliep verder. Het was dinsdag. Dan maar zelf.
p12.narration: We ran to Professor Otto, right at the top of the tower. He was asleep. I called, Hazel knocked, and Bruno barked so loudly that dust fell from the ceiling. Professor Otto opened one eye, mumbled that owls work at night, but not on Tuesdays, and went back to sleep. It was Tuesday. We would have to do it ourselves.

shots.prompt: Characters in this shot: Marcel (the grey British Shorthair cat with orange eyes, wearing tiny round wire-rimmed glasses); Hazel (a small hedgehog who always carries a tiny stack of old books); Bruno (a clumsy, cheerful basset hound puppy with very long ears). A round tower study full of old books and brass instruments. Professor Otto sleeps on his wooden perch, eyes closed, while below him Marcel calls up, Hazel knocks on the perch and Bruno barks; a little dust falls from the ceiling. Comedic.

p13.text: We kropen langs de hamster, die Bruno's buik nog altijd miste, en sprongen door het luik. Beneden fladderde een zwerm brokjes met vleugeltjes door de lucht. Honderden. Maar één ervan was de sleutel naar de volgende deur, zei Hazel: het brokje met de gebroken vleugel. Ik sprong, ik draaide, ik viel bijna, en ik ving het, zoals de Gouden Vlieg.
p13.narration: We crept past the hamster, who was still missing Bruno's belly, and jumped through the trapdoor. Below, a swarm of kibble with tiny wings fluttered through the air. Hundreds. But only one of them was the key to the next door, Hazel said: the piece with the broken wing. I jumped, I twisted, I almost fell, and I caught it, just like the Golden Fly.

shots.prompt: Characters in this shot: Marcel (the grey British Shorthair cat with orange eyes, wearing tiny round wire-rimmed glasses); Hazel (a small hedgehog who always carries a tiny stack of old books); Bruno (a clumsy, cheerful basset hound puppy with very long ears). A tall stone chamber below an open trapdoor, where hundreds of pieces of cat kibble with tiny feathered wings flutter through the air like a flock of birds. Marcel, Hazel and Bruno have just landed and look up in awe.

Characters in this shot: Marcel (the grey British Shorthair cat with orange eyes, wearing tiny round wire-rimmed glasses); Hazel (a small hedgehog who always carries a tiny stack of old books). Marcel leaps high through the fluttering swarm, mouth open, catching the one winged piece of kibble with a bent, broken wing, while Hazel points at it from below. Dynamic action, warm torchlight.

p14.text: De volgende kamer was een reusachtig schaakbord, met stenen katten zo groot als kasten. We moesten meespelen. Bruno werd een paard, Hazel een toren en ik de koning, wat ik niet meer dan logisch vond. Om te winnen moest iemand zich opofferen. Bruno stapte naar voren, zei met trillende stem dat we zonder hem verder moesten, en viel dramatisch om. Twee seconden later lag hij te snurken.
p14.narration: The next room was an enormous chessboard, with stone cats as big as wardrobes. We had to play along. Bruno became a knight, Hazel a castle, and I the king, which I found only logical. To win, someone had to sacrifice themselves. Bruno stepped forward, said in a trembling voice that we had to go on without him, and dramatically fell over. Two seconds later he was snoring.

shots.prompt: Characters in this shot: Marcel (the grey British Shorthair cat with orange eyes, wearing tiny round wire-rimmed glasses); Hazel (a small hedgehog who always carries a tiny stack of old books); Bruno (a clumsy, cheerful basset hound puppy with very long ears). A vast dark hall with a giant chessboard floor and huge stone cat statues as chess pieces. Marcel stands proudly on a square, chin up like a king; Hazel and Bruno stand on other squares, the stone pieces towering around them. Dramatic torchlight.

Characters in this shot: Bruno (a clumsy, cheerful basset hound puppy with very long ears); Marcel (the grey British Shorthair cat with orange eyes, wearing tiny round wire-rimmed glasses); Hazel (a small hedgehog who always carries a tiny stack of old books). Bruno lies dramatically on his back on a chess square, one paw on his chest, already fast asleep and snoring with a peaceful smile; Marcel and Hazel look on, moved.

p15.text: In de laatste gang sloegen paarse vlammen op, voor en achter ons. Op een tafel stonden zeven flesjes en een raadsel. Hazel dacht vier seconden na en wees het kleinste flesje aan. Er was maar genoeg voor één. Ze gaf het aan mij en zei dat ze toch te klein was voor heldendaden. Het smaakte naar tonijn en moed, en ik liep dwars door het vuur.
p15.narration: In the last corridor, purple flames rose up in front of us and behind us. On a table stood seven little bottles and a riddle. Hazel thought for four seconds and pointed at the smallest bottle. There was only enough for one. She handed it to me and said she was too small for heroics anyway. It tasted of tuna and courage, and I walked straight through the fire.

shots.prompt: Characters in this shot: Marcel (the grey British Shorthair cat with orange eyes, wearing tiny round wire-rimmed glasses); Hazel (a small hedgehog who always carries a tiny stack of old books). A narrow stone passage between walls of purple magical flames. Marcel and Hazel stand before a small wooden table with seven tiny glass bottles of different shapes and colours.

Characters in this shot: Hazel (a small hedgehog who always carries a tiny stack of old books); Marcel (the grey British Shorthair cat with orange eyes, wearing tiny round wire-rimmed glasses). Hazel holds up the smallest bottle to Marcel, both lit by purple firelight, a tender moment; behind Marcel a wall of purple flames waits.

p16.text: Achter het vuur lag de Steen der Brokjes op een sokkel, rood gloeiend, warm als een zonnige vensterbank. Ik nam hem in mijn poot. Op dat moment landde Corvus voor me, zijn vleugels wijd, zijn ogen als twee zwarte knikkers. Geef hem aan mij, fluisterde hij, en je krijgt een eigen etensbak, van goud, voor altijd. Een etensbak die nooit leeg raakt. Precies wat ik in de spiegel had gezien.
p16.narration: Behind the fire, the Kibble Stone lay on a pedestal, glowing red, warm as a sunny windowsill. I took it in my paw. At that moment Corvus landed in front of me, wings spread wide, eyes like two black marbles. Give it to me, he whispered, and you will have your own food bowl, made of gold, forever. A food bowl that never runs empty. Exactly what I had seen in the mirror.

shots.prompt: Characters in this shot: Marcel (the grey British Shorthair cat with orange eyes, wearing tiny round wire-rimmed glasses). A round stone chamber: Marcel stands by a stone pedestal with one paw on a small stone shaped like a piece of cat kibble, which glows warm red and lights up his whiskers and glasses.

Characters in this shot: Corvus (a large, glossy black raven with piercing eyes); Marcel (the grey British Shorthair cat with orange eyes, wearing tiny round wire-rimmed glasses). Corvus lands in front of Marcel with his wings spread wide, menacing, lit red from below by the glowing stone; Marcel looks torn, the reflection of a golden bowl in his glasses.

p17.text: Maar toen dacht ik aan Hazel, die me haar flesje gaf. Aan Bruno, snurkend op een schaakbord. Een volle buik is nog geen gelukkig hart. Ik draaide me om en rende, met de steen in mijn mond en Corvus vlak achter me, door het vuur, over het schaakbord, het luik uit. Daar stond Professor Otto, klaarwakker. Hij spreidde zijn vleugels en liet één oehoe horen, zo krachtig dat Corvus door het raam de nacht in werd geblazen.
p17.narration: But then I thought of Hazel, who gave me her bottle. Of Bruno, snoring on a chessboard. A full belly is not the same as a happy heart. I turned and ran, with the stone in my mouth and Corvus right behind me, through the fire, across the chessboard, out of the trapdoor. There stood Professor Otto, wide awake. He spread his wings and let out a single hoot, so powerful that Corvus was blown out of the window into the night.

shots.prompt: Characters in this shot: Marcel (the grey British Shorthair cat with orange eyes, wearing tiny round wire-rimmed glasses). Close-up of Marcel with his eyes closed, remembering; in a soft, dreamy glow around him, faint memories of Hazel holding up a bottle and Bruno asleep. Warm golden light.

Characters in this shot: Marcel (the grey British Shorthair cat with orange eyes, wearing tiny round wire-rimmed glasses); Corvus (a large, glossy black raven with piercing eyes). Marcel sprints across the giant chessboard with the glowing red stone in his mouth, Corvus swooping right behind him, dynamic motion blur.

Characters in this shot: Professor Otto (a large, wise old eagle-owl with fluffy ear tufts and amber eyes); Marcel (the grey British Shorthair cat with orange eyes, wearing tiny round wire-rimmed glasses); Corvus (a large, glossy black raven with piercing eyes). In a torchlit corridor, Professor Otto stands wide awake with his huge wings spread; Marcel skids to a stop in front of him, and behind them Corvus tumbles backwards out of an open arched window into the night sky, black feathers flying.

p18.text: Die avond was er een feestmaal in de grote zaal, met vis, taart en bergen brokjes. Huis Dutje won voor het eerst in duizend jaar de beker. Ze sliepen er allemaal doorheen. Bruno had taart op zijn neus, Hazel las een boek over mij, en ik mocht naast Professor Otto zitten. De steen bewaren we voortaan in de kelder, onder de mand, waar niemand ooit wakker genoeg is om hem te stelen. Ik was geen gewone kat meer.
p18.narration: That evening there was a feast in the great hall, with fish, cake and mountains of kibble. House Nap won the cup for the first time in a thousand years. They slept through all of it. Bruno had cake on his nose, Hazel read a book about me, and I got to sit next to Professor Otto. From now on, the stone is kept in the cellar, under the basket, where nobody is ever awake enough to steal it. I was no ordinary cat anymore.

shots.prompt: The great hall with hundreds of floating candles during a festive feast: long tables full of fish, cakes and bowls of kibble, a large golden cup on the table of animal students who are all fast asleep with their heads on the table.

p19.text: Weken later, thuis, lag ik op de vensterbank alsof er nooit iets gebeurd was. Om drie uur 's nachts begon het kattenluik weer te gloeien. Er viel een nieuwe brief door, met een zwarte veer eraan vast. Binnenkort op Marcelflix: Harry Pawter en de Kamer der Krabpalen.
